prompt:
Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2. Vanilla Minecraft blocks only, crisp voxel style, plain light background, no characters or animals. Two views side by side: LEFT straight-on north front elevation, orthographic; RIGHT north-east three-quarter view at the same scale. Skilled human builder quality: real massing, projecting details, recessed and framed openings, stepped block arches, real roof verges, eaves and ridge, stairs, slabs, fences, walls, trapdoors and lanterns. Keep both views consistent. No smooth non-block curves. Small view labels only.

Site: A big beige suburban McMansion on a cul-de-sac lot, seen from the street (north). 44 blocks wide, 32 deep, 2 storeys plus attic; main ridge y14, front gable y16, turret finial y17. The centrepiece is a tall white-trimmed front gable over a double-height portico: exactly four white quartz columns, a dark double front door with glass sidelights and an arched fanlight, a large arched Palladian window above it, and a half-round stepped-block window in the birch-beige gable. West (left in front elevation): octagonal two-storey turret bay with slate cone roof and lightning_rod finial. A big grey stone chimney rises up the west end wall. East (right): three-car garage wing, set back two blocks, exactly three dark spruce carriage doors made of spruce_trapdoor with glass_pane top lites, white headers, lanterns on stone piers, bonus room above with small shuttered windows. Lower front grey stone veneer up to white belt course; above it and on every other wall pale beige birch siding, white top plate and paired white quoins. Tall 2-wide arched windows with white sills and black shutters. Jumbled dark slate-grey asphalt-like hip roof built from deepslate, white dentil cornice, gable dormers at back, front gable and turret cone poking above. In front: wide pale concrete driveway, brick walk to portico steps, lamp posts, mailbox, clipped green lawn, podzol mulched beds with round voxel shrubs and tulips along foundation, one young birch. Behind: spruce deck with railing, smoker grill and patio table; show what is naturally visible without adding a third view or moving rear features to front.

changes: Generated with the built-in image tool and saved unchanged as concept.png in the current directory.
The two views are stacked vertically instead of side by side; their displayed scales differ.
The front elevation has slight visible depth and is not strictly orthographic.
Exact 44-by-32 dimensions, two-block garage setback, two-block window widths, and y14/y16/y17 heights cannot be verified. The main roof appears higher than the front gable.
The upper portico window is a single arched opening rather than a clearly articulated three-part Palladian window; the gable window is closer to a pointed arch than a half-round.
Two gable dormers were added to the front garage roof. A rear dormer is also visible.
Grey stone veneer extends around the visible east wall, although the plan calls for birch siding on other walls.
The garage doors resemble bespoke paneled carriage doors rather than an unambiguous assembly of vanilla spruce_trapdoor blocks.
An additional lightning_rod-like finial appears on the chimney, with a brown cap.
The birch is relatively mature, and several additional spruce-like trees were added behind the house.

A white patio umbrella was added above the rear table. Its thin canopy and some furniture details do not resolve cleanly into vanilla block geometry; white_carpet and oak_fence are inferred construction equivalents.
The mailbox has a tiny red flag that cannot be assigned a reliable exact block id from the image.
The brick steps require brick_stairs and brick_slab; paving edges suggest smooth_stone_slab. Additional trees require spruce_log and spruce_leaves.
Lamp posts are predominantly stone piers topped with lanterns.
The street is shown as a straight segment rather than an identifiable cul-de-sac.
Landscaping, lamp positions, and some architectural proportions vary between the two views.
Some window muntins, curved trim, shrubs, and small details are finer than clearly buildable vanilla geometry.

The roles retain every supplied plan block, including hidden interior blocks. Added ids and the objects list are visual interpretations and construction equivalents, not a recoverable exact block inventory; flower species, furniture parts, and the smoking grill assembly remain ambiguous.
